summary: Ray and Emma return from an early dinner and an evening stroll to the observation deck, where they kissed beneath a meteor, which she claimed was good luck. Ray, who has grown sentimental about her, accepts her invitation into her quarters to meet her children's household. Emma explains that Amah designs the children's education schedule and tutors carry it out, and that she is only there for moral support. Ray is reluctant to face Amah again after an awkward prior meeting, but agrees to meet the children, who are finishing evening studies.
one_line: Ray accepts Emma's invitation into her household, where he expects to meet her children and the awkward matriarch Amah.
key_facts: Ray had an early dinner with Emma, during which he told her about his supposed job and Ziggy riding his ass for his screw-ups.
Ray suspects Emma was only pretending to be interested in his job talk, though she seemed genuinely to care.
After dinner, Emma and Ray strolled up to the obs deck to count stars and galactic clusters.
Emma said kissing beneath the tail of a passing meteor was good luck, which Ray suspects she made up on the spot.
Emma invites Ray in for a while, saying it would make Amah feel more comfortable with him.
Ray says his schedule has become a bit more flexible lately.
Emma says Ray's previous meeting with Amah was a little awkward.
Ray has no interest in talking to Amah again and does not care much about her or Frederick.
Ray says he would like to meet the kids who occupy so much of Emma's time, to assure himself they actually exist.
Emma says Amah designs the schedule for the children's education and the tutors she selected to travel with them implement it.
Emma says she is just there for moral support and is not very good with children.
Emma keys in her entry code at the door, stopping the kako-daemon's warble.
Ray had been wondering how to let go of Emma's hand without seeming to avoid holding it in front of Amah and the Whiston domestics.
Ray compares this romantic dilemma to one unchanged since Julie Gentry, twenty years earlier.
